einzeiler: Physicist Jim Al-Khalili discusses time, quantum mechanics, and biology.
kurzfassung: Sean Carroll and Jim Al-Khalili explore the fundamental nature of time, its directionality, and its relationship with thermodynamics. They examine how open systems and quantum entanglement shape our understanding of reality and biology. The conversation highlights persistent mysteries in physics that continue to intrigue researchers.
stichpunkte: Time is analyzed as a tangible, four-dimensional element of reality rather than a mere human construct.
The arrow of time is viewed through the lens of open systems, challenging traditional strictly time-symmetric equations.
The past hypothesis remains essential for explaining why the early universe possessed exceptionally low entropy.
Biological processes like photosynthesis and DNA mutation may actively utilize non-trivial quantum mechanics.
Quantum decoherence and entanglement help explain the transition from quantum possibilities to single measurement outcomes.
Emergent time concepts suggest that while time might arise from deeper principles, it remains a real phenomenon for observers within the universe.

clips.text: The guest argues that the directional flow of time is inherently baked into the fabric of the universe rather than merely being a psychological illusion.
Standard time-symmetric dynamical equations fail to represent reality fully because absolute isolation does not exist anywhere in nature.

clips.hook: The sun functions as a low entropy engine
clips.text: Nuclear fusion continuously powers stellar output, allowing stars to supply the steady stream of low entropy required to sustain complex structures.

clips.hook: Decoherence removes interference without deciding outcomes
clips.text: Environmental interactions eliminate quantum overlap and superposition, but they leave behind distinct possibilities rather than forcing a single actual result.

clips.hook: Avian navigation relies on quantum mechanics
clips.text: Migratory birds manage to sense the Earth's weak magnetic field by utilizing sensitive pairs of entangled electrons located within specialized molecules in their eyes.

beschreibung:
Everyone lives through time, but we continue to struggle to fully understand it. We remain unsure whether time is fundamental or emergent, why it has an arrow pointing from past to future, and how that arrow connects to our experience of time's passage. Jim Al-Khalili's new book is On Time: The Physics that Makes the Universe Tick. We discuss what time is at the most basic level, and how it connects to open questions in biology, cosmology, and quantum mechanics.

Jim Al-Khalili received his Ph.D. in physics from the University of Surrey. He is currently Distinguished Emeritus Professor of Physics at Surrey. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society, and has served as past president of the British Science Association. He has been awarded the Michael Faraday Prize by the Royal Society, and has been appointed an appointed Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
